Run the subsamples for a learning curve

Source: R/learning_subsample.R
learning_subsample.Rd

Calls randomForestSRC::subsample() once per fraction, with performance = TRUE, and optionally once more as a double bootstrap for the whole cohort, and returns the list that gg_learning() tidies. It records the stratify setting on each result, which subsample() itself does not keep, so gg_learning() can report the number of events in each refit as exact rather than assumed.

Usage

learning_subsample(
  object,
  fractions = c(0.125, 0.25, 0.5),
  replicates = 20L,
  bootstrap = TRUE,
  stratify = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A randomForestSRC forest (class rfsrc), grown with the settings the refits should copy.

fractions

Fractions of the cohort to refit on, each greater than 0 and less than 1.

replicates

Positive whole number; refits per fraction, passed to subsample() as B.

bootstrap

Logical; also run the double bootstrap for the whole cohort (fraction 1). Defaults to TRUE. Left out, with a warning, when object imputed missing values (na.action = "na.impute" on data with any missing value): randomForestSRC crashes R double-bootstrapping such a forest. The subsamples are unaffected.

stratify

Logical; passed to subsample(), which samples within each class (or survival status) when TRUE, its default.

...

Further arguments to subsample(), such as importance.

Value

A list of subsample() results, one per fraction in increasing order and the bootstrap last (when it is run), each carrying a stratify attribute.

Details

This is the expensive step: it grows replicates forests per fraction, plus as many for the bootstrap, each the size of object. Run it once, save the result and pass it to gg_learning() as often as needed.

subsample() draws its subsamples with R's random number generator, so set the seed before calling this function for a reproducible curve.

See also

gg_learning(), randomForestSRC::subsample().

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- randomForestSRC::rfsrc(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, ntree = 50,
                              importance = "permute", seed = -1)
set.seed(1)
subsamples <- learning_subsample(fit, fractions = c(0.25, 0.5),
                                 replicates = 5)
curve <- gg_learning(subsamples, top_k = 3, min_events = 10)
summary(curve)
#>   fraction  n events   counts B error_mean  error_sd jaccard     kendall
#> 1     0.25  8      8    exact 5   35.78079 22.852897    0.68          NA
#> 2     0.50 16     16    exact 5   13.80185  4.501053    0.38  0.03333333
#> 3     1.00 32     32 expected 5   10.88033  1.889053    0.49 -0.06000000
#>   low_events optimistic
#> 1       TRUE      FALSE
#> 2      FALSE      FALSE
#> 3      FALSE      FALSE
# }
